capacityPolicy.source: Confluence SOP: Resource Planning, Jira Management and Tempo Time Logging

MT-1091.why: Parent for the Marketplace register. On 23 Sep four children were closed with reasons and four (MT-1092, MT-1093, MT-1096, MT-1101) stopped appearing in Jira. Only MT-1094 is still open.
MT-1091.action: Record what happened to MT-1092, MT-1093, MT-1096 and MT-1101, and decide on MT-1094.

MT-1092.why: Azure AD B2C tenant is live. Marketplace login works in production and Identity is now removing token claims (ID-679 to ID-686).

MT-1093.why: 27 AI-server listings for Dell, HPE, NVIDIA, Supermicro and Lenovo were moved to production between 16 and 22 Sep. The register's own mitigation says to block publication until OEM agreements are confirmed.
MT-1093.action: Confirm OEM agreement status per brand before products are enabled.

MT-1094.why: Financing modal was part of the PDP story (MT-1217), which closed on 24 Sep. No Jira evidence that Gynger sandbox access was obtained.
MT-1094.action: Confirm whether financing is in go-live scope. If not, close. If yes, assign an owner.

MT-1095.why: Closed 23 Sep by Shashi Prasad K: CDN is up and serving product images for all migrated products (MT-1528).

MT-1096.why: Still valid for checkout go-live. Untouched and unassigned for 78 days.
MT-1096.action: Assign to Identity lead and link to USP-3751, which covers the same outage.

MT-1097.why: Closed 23 Sep by Shashi Prasad K: payments are recorded manually, so the online payment-gateway feature is being deprecated.
MT-1097.action: Revisit only if an online payment gateway is brought back into scope.

MT-1098.why: Closed 23 Sep by Shashi Prasad K: every catalogue product is sold as request-for-quote, so no OEM list price is shown to buyers.
MT-1098.action: Reopen if any product is enabled with a fixed listed price.

MT-1099.why: Mitigation delivered. Event-based sync, manual order sync and admin point adjustment exist (comment 16 Sep). Ticket is Done.

MT-1100.why: Closed 23 Sep. Marketplace reads user details from the userinfo API instead of token claims (7 Sep). Identity claim-removal subtasks ID-679 to ID-683 sit in another project.
MT-1100.action: Confirm with Security that ID-679 to ID-683 reached production.

MT-1101.why: Marketing site shipped GDPR cookie consent (MR-760, Done). No equivalent evidence for Marketplace.
MT-1101.action: Confirm Marketplace consent coverage, then close or assign.

EN-16.why: Notification Service register has had no owner and no update since 7 Jul.
EN-16.action: Assign an engineering owner this week or formally accept the risks.

EN-17.why: High likelihood and high impact. No automated tests. Unowned for 78 days.
EN-17.action: Assign owner and add to next sprint.

EN-18.why: SQL injection via string interpolation. High likelihood, critical impact. Unowned for 78 days.
EN-18.action: Treat as a security defect, not a register entry. Fix before any further Notification Service release.

EN-19.why: Public mutation endpoints accept writes without auth. High likelihood, critical impact. Unowned for 78 days.
EN-19.action: Treat as a security defect. Fix before any further Notification Service release.

EN-20.why: Deployment still runs outside the repo pipeline. Unowned for 78 days.
EN-20.action: Assign to DevOps with a date.

IN-985.why: Parent epic for the Devops register.
IN-985.action: Close once IN-986 load-test evidence is attached.

IN-986.why: Horizontal pod autoscaling configured in production at 80% CPU (3 Sep). Ticket is Done. Load testing before release is not evidenced.
IN-986.action: Close risk. Keep 'load test before each production release' as a release checklist item.

USP-3746.why: USP register is actively owned. Children updated 17 Sep with 30 Sep due dates.

USP-3747.action: Run the periodic auth-bypass audit named in the mitigation.

USP-3748.action: Confirm partner API access before Phase 3.

USP-3750.why: Depends on Rewards API. Same failure mode as MT-1099, which Marketplace has already mitigated.
USP-3750.action: Reuse the Marketplace sync and reconciliation pattern.

USP-3751.action: Now the only open identity-outage risk, since MT-1096 no longer appears in Jira. Extend it to cover Marketplace login.

USP-3753.action: Confirm the failure mode applies to the advisory workflow.

USP-3755.why: Scope creep is visible now: 198 USP issues created in 30 days and 59 open bugs, including 5 S1 bugs raised on 25 and 28 Sep and still in To Do.
USP-3755.action: Enforce the change-request gate named in the mitigation.

reportedRisksNotInJira.title: Hiring a Product Catalog resource
evidence: Suganya Murugaraj researched and validated attribute values for Dell, HPE, Supermicro and Lenovo between 15 and 22 Sep (PC-133). She has now moved on to NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
Naman Bapna created 27 AI-server listings on UAT and moved them all to production between 16 and 22 Sep (MT-1500 to MT-1512, MT-1528).
The Confluence 30/60/90 plan for the Product Research & Upload team already defines the roles this hire would fill.
reportedRisksNotInJira.replaceWith: Key-person dependency on Naman Bapna for Magento product creation and production migration. One researcher (Suganya) covers all brands.
reportedRisksNotInJira.action: Cross-train one more person on CSV import and production migration before the NVIDIA Vera Rubin batch. Revisit hiring only if the pipeline grows past current throughput.

newRisks.title: Key-person dependency on Magento product migration
newRisks.detail: Every UAT product creation and every UAT-to-production migration was done by one person, including the 8 Vera Rubin products created on 25 Sep and moved to production on 28 Sep (MT-1532, MT-1535).
newRisks.mitigation: Pair a second engineer on the next batch and document the CSV and attribute steps as an SOP.

newRisks.title: AI-server products are in production but disabled
newRisks.detail: All 35 migrated listings, including the 8 Vera Rubin products moved on 28 Sep, were verified and then disabled pending business approval. The UAT cross-validation closed on 28 Sep.
newRisks.mitigation: Set an approval date with the approver and a named enablement owner.

newRisks.title: Marketplace staging performance
newRisks.detail: Lighthouse performance score on staging was 43 on 18 Sep, after categories were reduced. The ticket was routed to the wrong person first.
newRisks.mitigation: Performance baseline and fix plan before enabling products.

newRisks.title: Sitemap exposes 250 of 500+ URLs
newRisks.detail: The production sitemap lists 250 URLs. More than 500 are expected. This hurts SEO and caps automated test coverage.
newRisks.mitigation: Fix the sitemap generator, then extend Playwright coverage to the full URL list.

newRisks.title: Time-logging data cannot support utilisation reporting
newRisks.detail: Every Tempo worklog in the window uses the generic description 'time-tracking'. Marketing content, Design, Infrastructure and Hamara CRM have no Tempo hours against Jira at all.
newRisks.mitigation: Enforce the SOP rule that a description is mandatory. Pull the weekly utilisation view from Tempo by worker, not by Jira assignee.

newRisks.title: Marketplace QA automation has no owner
newRisks.detail: The end-to-end automation framework was moved to backlog after the assigned engineer left on 23 Jul. Web-Marketing has working Playwright automation (MR-1165) that could be reused.
newRisks.mitigation: Reuse the Web-Marketing Playwright setup for a Marketplace smoke suite.

issues.title: Policy change identified during UAT is not recorded anywhere in Jira
issues.impact: Not measurable from Jira. The change is not logged, so its effect on scope, dates and effort cannot be traced.
issues.rootCause: No change-request ticket type, and no UAT sign-off step that captures business-policy changes. About 300 tickets mentioning policy or change requests across 8 projects were checked. The closest are the returns-policy use cases (MT-1116, MT-1180, MT-1181, MT-1187) and MT-1286, which made the return-eligibility window configurable on 2 Sep. None of them records a change found in UAT.
issues.preventive: Log it now as a Change Request with impact and effort, linked to the affected stories. Add a 'business rules confirmed' line to UAT sign-off covering returns, refunds, loyalty points and pricing. Open business-rule questions already exist on MT-978 (loyalty points) and MT-1488 (refund and exchange timelines).

issues.title: AI Factory final prices calculated wrongly in production
issues.impact: The subscription price API returns the wrong final price for every billing and term combination in the Traditional, Modular and Nuclear AI Factory. One logged example expected 174,420 and got 150,660, about 14% low. A separate S1 has the Document API failing with a 502 on the first request.
issues.rootCause: Not recorded yet. The Document API failure is suspected to be the API gateway blocking the first request (comment on USP-4231, 28 Sep).
issues.actionTaken: All three are S1, still in To Do on 29 Sep, and now due 30 Sep. No fix recorded.
issues.preventive: Add the price-calculation checks to the automated regression run before each production release.

issues.title: Four Marketplace register items no longer appear in Jira, including the red OEM-agreement dependency
issues.impact: MT-1093 (OEM/brand partner agreements before listing) was rated red while 27 AI-server listings sit in production. With the ticket gone there is no record of whether OEM agreements were confirmed. MT-1096 (identity outage) and MT-1101 (GDPR/CCPA cookie handling) were still open.
issues.rootCause: A search by key returns none of the four tickets, so they were deleted or moved where this account cannot see them. The four items closed the same evening (MT-1095, MT-1097, MT-1098, MT-1100) each got a closing comment. These four did not.
issues.preventive: Close register items with a reason instead of deleting them. Record the OEM-agreement decision for each brand before any listing is enabled.

issues.title: Marketplace scope changed mid-sprint to AI servers only
issues.impact: A 38-task category-disable plan was added on 10 Sep. 36 are done and about 43 hours were logged against it. The home page is being redesigned around B300, GB300 and Vera Rubin (MT-1524, due 30 Sep).
issues.actionTaken: Category disable executed in 12 days. URL disposition (MT-1447) and performance check (MT-1475) remain open.
issues.preventive: Route strategy changes through a change request with an impact estimate before tasks are raised.

issues.title: Dell products created with wrong parent-child configuration
issues.impact: 4 of 6 Dell products needed rework. One had to be recreated. Dell GPU values also needed correction (PC-133, 17 Sep).
issues.rootCause: No agreed standard for configurable versus standalone products before creation started.
issues.actionTaken: Fixed and verified on UAT on 17 Sep. Later brands were created as standalone products.
issues.preventive: Apply the pre-publish QA checklist in the Confluence 30/60/90 plan to every batch before production migration.

issues.title: Product list and specs arrived late
issues.impact: HPE creation waited a day for one product's details. Timelines could not be set until the final list existed.
issues.rootCause: Creation started before the approved product list was final.
issues.preventive: Require a signed approved-product list per batch before creation, as the 30/60/90 plan's approval gate specifies.

issues.title: Migrated products are disabled pending approval
issues.impact: 35 listings are in production but not visible to buyers: 27 since 18–22 Sep and 8 Vera Rubin since 28 Sep.
issues.rootCause: Approval step sits after migration, with no date.
issues.actionTaken: Cross-validation on UAT closed on 28 Sep (MT-1529). A full catalogue re-check is due 30 Sep (PC-136).
issues.preventive: Put a dated approval gate in the plan for each batch.

issues.title: Earlier Lenovo UAT products not visible, and ticket status not maintained
issues.impact: A manually created Lenovo product did not appear on the UAT storefront. PC-121 is still 'To Do' with 49.5 hours logged. It is not clear whether its Lenovo products were superseded by the 2 Lenovo products in MT-1512.
issues.preventive: Close or re-scope PC-121 and state which Lenovo SKUs are in the go-live list.

issues.title: Staging performance score of 43
issues.impact: Slow pages on the reduced catalogue. Risk to conversion and SEO at go-live.
issues.rootCause: Not yet analysed. The ticket was first routed to the wrong person.
issues.actionTaken: Reassigned to Naveen Jangid on 22 Sep. Now in UAT/staging (last updated 23 Sep). No new score recorded.
issues.preventive: Add a performance budget to the release checklist.

issues.title: Production sitemap lists 250 of 500+ URLs
issues.impact: Search engines and the Playwright suite both see only half the site.
issues.rootCause: Sitemap generation limit. Not yet confirmed.
issues.preventive: Add a URL-count check to the automated smoke run.

issues.title: Marketplace buyer stories were past due
issues.impact: Home page, product listing and PDP were due 31 Aug and closed on 24–25 Sep, 24 to 25 days late. Account hub (MT-1311) and returns flow (MT-1331) were due 15 Sep and are still in testing.
issues.rootCause: Not recorded. Due dates were not re-baselined after the AI-servers pivot.
issues.actionTaken: MT-1216 and MT-1217 closed 24 Sep, MT-1215 closed 25 Sep. Account hub is 4 of 10 subtasks done (3 on 29 Sep); returns is 10 of 12, in testing.
issues.preventive: Re-baseline due dates when scope changes, per the SOP's Scenario 14.

issues.title: Marketplace automation framework parked after a resource exit
issues.rootCause: Single owner left and work was not reassigned.
issues.preventive: Reuse the Web-Marketing Playwright suite and name a new owner.

issues.title: Conflicting requirement on live chat
issues.impact: The team was asked to build a widget that it had earlier been asked to remove.
issues.rootCause: Requirement changes are not recorded as decisions.
issues.actionTaken: Waiting on chatbot design and APIs.
issues.preventive: Keep a decision log per project and link reversals to the original decision.

utilisationNotes.attributionWarning: Tempo writes every worklog to Jira under its own app account, so Jira cannot say who logged an hour. Hours here are credited to each ticket's current assignee. When a developer's ticket is handed to QA, the developer's hours move with it. Any day above 10 hours for one person is flagged for this reason.
utilisationNotes.overheadGap: Meetings, stand-ups and leave are logged on 13 shared overhead tickets in Uvation Projects, which is outside this report's scope, so that time is not in these totals.

deepDives.finding: Logged 40.5 hours on 10 days, all on PC-133. That averages about 4 hours a day against an 8-hour day, or 51% of the 80-hour capacity. 15 Sep shows 1.5 hours and 28 Sep 0.5 hours.
deepDives.context: The 5.5 hours on 17 Sep covered Dell GPU corrections with Naman and then HPE validation, which is 3 products. Each product also needed a tech-spec table, long description, short description and product-card copy in HTML. Between 15 and 24 Sep she validated 19 products for 4 brands and started the 8 Vera Rubin products, about 1.5 hours per product.
deepDives.question: Where are the other 3 or so hours a day? They may be on overhead tickets, which Jira hides, or unlogged.
deepDives.verify: Pull Suganya's Tempo timesheet for 15–28 Sep and compare the total with 80 hours. The full catalogue re-check (PC-136) she started on 29 Sep is due 30 Sep.

deepDives.finding: Jira credits Sapavat with 96.8 hours, 121% of the 80-hour capacity, with six days between 11 and 15.5 hours (15–17, 24, 25 and 28 Sep). That is not plausible for one person and shows developer time on tickets reassigned to QA.
deepDives.context: Sapavat's own QA tasks show 0.5 to 2 hours each. For example, the navigation, homepage-module and facet UI updates for the category disable took 1 hour each (MT-1455 to MT-1457). Functional test on staging took 1.5 hours and the toggle test 1.5 hours (MT-1471, MT-1473).
deepDives.question: Sapavat's real hours cannot be separated from developer hours in Jira. The Tempo worker report is the only reliable source.
deepDives.verify: Pull Sapavat's Tempo timesheet by worker. Check that QA time is logged on QA subtasks, not on development subtasks.
